title: Legislative districts of Aklan
wikitext:
{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Aklan''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Aklan]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[Aklan's 1st congressional district|first]] and [[Aklan's 2nd congressional district|second]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative districts of Capiz}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Aklan were represented under the [[Capiz's at-large congressional district|at-large district]] of the province of [[Capiz]] in the [[Malolos Congress]] from 1898 to 1899. These were later represented under the [[Capiz's 2nd congressional district|2nd]] and [[Capiz's 3rd congressional district|3rd]] districts of Capiz from 1907 to 1941. In the disruption caused by the [[World War II]], these were represented as part of the at-large district of Capiz in the [[National Assembly (Second Philippine Republic)|National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic]] from 1943 to 1944; the pre-war districts were restored in 1945. Republic Act No. 1414, enacted on April 25, 1956, created the province of [[Aklan]] from the western, [[Aklanon language|Aklanon]]-speaking municipalities of Capiz.{{Cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=1414|date=April 25, 1956 |title=An Act to Create the Province of Aklan |url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/15_republicacts.php?id=1416 |access-date=August 4, 2019 |website=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library}} The new province began to elect a separate representative under its [[Aklan's at-large congressional district|lone district]] starting in the [[1957 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1957 elections]]. Aklan was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region VI]] from 1978 to 1984. The province returned one representative, elected at-large, to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province constituted a lone district{{Cite web |last=1986 Constitutional Commission |date=February 2, 1987 |title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance |url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/ |access-date=November 19, 2017 |website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines}} which elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. The signing of Republic Act No. 11077 authored by [[Carlito S. Marquez]] on September 24, 2018{{Cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=11077 |publisher=Congress of the Philippines |date=September 24, 2018 |title=An Act Reapportioning the Province of Aklan into Two (2) Legislative Districts |url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/downloads/2018/09sep/20180924-RA-11077-RRD.pdf |access-date=August 4, 2019}} reapportioned Aklan into two legislative districts, which elected their separate representatives starting in the [[2019 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2019 elections]]. == Senatorial representation == {{further|Philippines's 7th senatorial district}} Between 1916 and 1935, the territory of what is now Aklan (then part of the province of [[Capiz]]) was represented in the [[Senate of the Philippines]] through the [[Philippines's 7th senatorial district|7th senatorial district of the Philippine Islands]]. However, in 1935, all senatorial districts were abolished when a unicameral [[National Assembly of the Philippines|National Assembly]] was installed under a new constitution following the passage of the [[Tydings–McDuffie Act]], which established the [[Commonwealth of the Philippines]]. Since the [[1941 Philippine Senate election|1941 elections]], when the Senate was restored after a [[1940 Philippine constitutional plebiscites|constitutional plebiscite]], all twenty-four members of the upper house have been elected countrywide [[at-large]]. == Congressional representation == {{main|Aklan's 1st congressional district|Aklan's 2nd congressional district|Aklan's at-large congressional district}} Aklan has been represented in the lower house of [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various Philippine national legislatures]] since 1898, through its [[Aklan's 1st congressional district|first]] and [[Aklan's 2nd congressional district|second congressional district]]s. == Provincial board districts == {{main|Aklan Provincial Board}} The municipalities of Aklan are represented in the [[Aklan Provincial Board]], the [[Sangguniang Panlalawigan]] (provincial legislature) of the province, through Aklan's first and second provincial board districts. == Current districts and representatives == {{columns-list|colwidth=10em|}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative districts and congressional representatives of [[Aklan]] |- !District ! colspan="3" |Current representative !
